oma: [uma + a. ] (ti) CL=7 [Dhāna, ṭī.770.ava+amaca. Kotthubha. Ava+mā+a. Visuddhi, ṭī. Avama(saṃ)] (1) One who is inferior. One who is poor. (3) A little. Get less. Tiny. Small. Decrease.
omadda: [ava + madda + hi] (kri) CL=7 May you cause to come down. May you oppress. See - Omaddati (B).
[ava + madda + a.] (pu) CL=7 [Avamadaṃ(saṃ)] You afflict and oppress. See below.
omaddakāraka: [omadda + kāraka] (ti) CL=7 One who overwhelms and oppresses.
omaddanti: [ava + mudda + a + anti] (kri) CL=7 (A) They step on or crush. (B) They cause to place down. They cause to come down. They suppress. They oppress. See - Omuddati (A) (B).
omaddanā: [ava + madda + yu + ā (itthīpaccaññaḥ) avamadaṃna(saṃ)] (thī) CL=7 Oppression. See - Omadditvā (A).
omaddati: [ava + madda + a + ti] (kri) CL=7 (A) He steps on or crushes. (B) He causes to place down. He causes to come down. He oppresses.
omaddita: [ava + madda + ta] (ti) CL=7 Should be oppressed.
omadditvā: [ava + madda + tvā] (kri, vi) CL=7 (A) Having suppressed. Having suppressed with words (sound). (B) Having overwhelmed. (C) Having oppressed. (D) Having massaged. Having crushed.
omajphati: [ava + majja + a + ti] (kri) CL=7 (He) reviews or (he) concentrates and contemplates.
omaka: [oma + ka.] (ti) CL=7 [Uma-nindāyaṃ, kammea, saketthe ko, usso. Dhāna, ṭī. 770.] (1) gets less. Decrease. (2) A decrease amount. Tiny. One who is short and bent legs. (3) One who is inferior. (3) (Kilesā) that has the decreased power.
omakacā: [omaka + cā(ca)tumāsa] (ca)tumāsa (ti) CL=7 Less than four months.
omakadassa: [omaka + disa + a] (ti) CL=7 Sees a small-sized. See decreased size. One who has a view of decreasing.
omakadesanā: [omakā + dessanā] (thī) CL=7 A sermon that preaches incomplete status.
omakaparimāṇa: [omaka + parimāṇa] (ti) CL=7 With a small amount.
omakapatta: [omaka + patta] (pu) CL=7 An alms bowl that is smaller than normal size. A small alms bowl. A small alms bowl.
omakapañña: [omakā + paññā] (ti) CL=7 One who has low knowledge.
omakappamāṇa: [omaka + pamāṇa] (na) CL=7 (1) A small amount. (maaū, sya.). A tiny. (bhāsā, ṭī.)(ti) (2) One who has a decreased amount (of something).
omakasattasammata: [omakasatta + sammata] (ti) CL=7 Should be known as who is an inferior being.
omakkhi: [u(ava)+makkha+i]  CL=9 (the doctrine) which is flattered and abandoned- rejected.
omakomaka: [omaka + omaka] (ti) CL=7 Which is smaller than a small size. (An alms bowl) which is very small.
omakukkaṭṭha: [omaka + ukkaṭṭha] (ti) CL=7 Which is smaller than one. (An alms bowl) who is smaller than the biggest size.
omapañña: [omā + paññā] (ti) CL=7 With less wisdom. One who has less wisdom.
omasa: [ava + masa + ṇa] (pu) CL=7 A cause of provoking ears and heart. Unpleasant to listen. (Words (sound)) that is coarse words or rude words. See - Omasavāda (1).
omasana: [ata + masa + yu] (thī, na) CL=7 (thī) (1) Fondles to lower place. Puts down. (Na) (2) Speaks rude words that pierce the ears and heart. Speaks coarsely.
omasanasambhava: [omasana + sambhava] (pu) CL=7 The origin of speaking rude words that pierce the ears and heart. The origin of speaking coarsely.
omasanavatthu: [omasana + vatthu] (na) CL=7 A story that is about speaking coarsely that pierces the ears and heart.
omasanta: [ava + masa + a + anta] (ti) CL=7 (1) One who considers to descend. (2) One who speaks coarsely that pierce the ears and heart.
omasanti: [ava + masa + a + anti] (kri) CL=7 (1) They speak coarsely that pierce the ears and heart. See - Omasati (1). (2) They eat. See - Omasati (2).
omasatha: [ava + masa + a + tha] (kri) CL=7 May you (pl) speak words (sound) that pierce the ears and heart. May you (pl) speak coarsely. See - Omasati (1).
omasati: [ava + masa + a + ti.] (kri) CL=7 [Nīti, dhā. 174. Avamasၐti (saṃ)] (1) Words (sound) that pierce the ears and heart (means rude words). He speaks coarsely. He insults. He speaks rude words. (pācita, say.) Which is piercing the ears and heart.  (sārattha.) Which pierces the ears and heart. (kaṅkhā, ṭī, saca.) (2) He considers. He considers the lower portion or state. (saddattha.) He eats. (adhippāyattha).
omasavāda: [omasa + vāda] (pu) CL=7 (1) Rude words (sound) that pierce the ears and heart. Coarse words (sound). Abuse words (sound). (2) Speaks coarsely that pierce the ears and heart. (Ti) (3) An offense due to speaking coarsely. One who has an offense for speaking rude words (sound).
omasavādagarahaṇa: [omasavāda + garahaṇa]  CL=10 Insulting, slandering, slandering, slandering, which pierces the ear and the heart.
omasavādapācittiya: [omasavāda + pācittiya] (na) CL=7 One who has an offense for speaking coarsely that pierces the ears and heart.
omasavādasikkhāpada: [omasavāda + sikkhāpada] (na) CL=7 A vinaya rule that rules for insulting or speaking rude words that pierce the ears and heart. Omasavāda vinaya rule.
omasissanti: [ava + masa + ssanti] (kri) CL=7 They will speak coarsely that pierces the ears and heart. They will speak rude words. See - Omasati (1).
omasissatha: [ava + masa + ssatha] (kri) CL=7 You (pl) will speak coarsely that pierces the ears and heart. You (pl) will speak rude words. See - Omasati (1).
omasitukāma: [omasituṃ + kamu + ṇa] (ti) CL=7 One who wants to speak rude words that pierce the ears and heart.
omasitvā: [ava + masa + tvā] (kri, vi) CL=7 Having picked up or having considered or having fondled.
omasiṃsu: [ava + masa + uuṃ] (kri) CL=7 They spoke rude words. They spoke coarsely. See -
omatta: [(ava+mattā=)omattā + ṇa] (ti) CL=7 With a lesser amount. One who has less power.
[oma + tta] (na) CL=7 (1) As one who is inferior. (2) As one who is poor.
omaññanā: [ava + maññanā] (thī) CL=7 Thinks that which is inferior. Perceives that is a low status or an inferior.
omaññitatta: [ava + maññitatta] (na) CL=7 As one who is inferior. As the perception of one who is inferior. See - Omaññanā.
omaṭṭha: [ava + masa + ta] (na) CL=7 (1) Which mouth or face is facing downward. (Ti) (2) One who should be provoked from top to down. (One who should be provoked from his head to feet).
omeha: [ava + miha + a] (pu, na) CL=7 Diabetes disease.
omissakaparisā: [omissakā + parisā] (thī) CL=7 The intermingled audiences or crowded audiences.
omuddhaka: [ava + muddha + ka] (ti) CL=7 One who is with the head hanging down.
omukhanikkhittapaṇṇakosasaṇṭhāna: [omukhanikkhittapaṇṇakosa + saṇṭhāna] (ti) CL=7 The appearance is like a leaf that is placed face down.
omukka: [ava + muca + ta.] (ti) CL=7 [Omuccatīti omukkā. Upāhanā. Rū, nhā. 378. Viyo-ge omukkaupāhano. Rū, nhā. 128.] (1) Takes off and gives up. has been worn and taken off. (bhāsā, ṭī.) (The old sandals or shoes) that have been worn and taken off. (2) One who stands on the shoes. (3) One who should be taken off and given up.
[o + muca + ta] (ti) CL=7 Should be put on or worn.
omukkamakuṭa: [omukka + makuṭa] (ti) CL=7 One who wears or puts on the crown.
omuttenthi: [ava + mutta + ṇe + anti] (kri) CL=7 They discharge urine. See - Omutteti.
omutteti: [ava + mutta + ṇe + ti.] (kri) CL=7 [Nīti, dhā. 309. Avamūtrayati (saṃ)] He discharges urine.
omuttika: [(ava + mutti=) omutti + ka] (ti) CL=7 One who discharges urine. See - Ohadita.
omuucanta: [ava + muca + a + anta] (ti) CL=7 One who takes off.
omuucate: [ava + muca + a + tha] (kri) CL=7 Takes off. See - Omuucati.
omuucatha: [ava + muca + a + tha]  CL=9 May you (pl) take off. See - Omuñcati.
omuucati: [ava + muca + a + ti] (kri) CL=7 Takes off.
omuuci: [ava + muca + ī] (kri) CL=7 (He) took off. See - Omuucati.
omuucitvā: [ava + muca + tvā] (kri, vi) CL=7 Having taken off. Having given up.
omuucāpetvā: [ava + muca + ṇāpe + tvā] (kri, vi) CL=7 Having caused to take off.
omuñceyyaṃ: [ava + muca + eyyaṃ]  CL=9 They would take off. See - Omuñcati.
omāna: [ava + māna + a]  CL=9 (1) Inferior pride; Humble pride. Pride of those who are inferior. When one is humble 'I am an inferior one of those who are inferior in terms of caste, etc.,' there arises the pride of taking oneself as "I'. This is called "omāna". The belittling of others on oneself as "an inferior one" is also called 'omāna'. Netti, ṭtha. 253. Mūlaṭī, 1. 121. Anuṭī,1.128. Mūlaṭī,3.221. Anuṭī,3,297.) (2) Being too proud, Being with total disregard, arrogant. (Just 'atimāna' is called 'omāna' because it is inferior.)'
omānapahāna: [omāna + pahāna] (na) CL=7 Giving up māna that is inferior.
omāti: [ava + mā + a + ti.] (kri) CL=7 [Saṃ, ṭī. Omā+a+ti. Nīti, dhā. 131.] He is capable (of).
omasisu: [ava + masa + uuṃ] (kri) CL=7 They spoke rude words. They spoke coarsely. See -
omuñceyya: [ava + muca + eyyaṃ]  CL=9 They would take off. See - Omuñcati.
